implemented_capabilities.capability: Prerequisite-staircase graph tools over Common Core standards
implemented_capabilities.notes: Hand-written parameterized Cypher over Standard/SubArea/Student nodes: variable-length PROGRESSES_TO predecessor walk (depth clamped to MAX_DEPTH, depth interpolated as an int after clamping), shortestPath climb to the student's grade, algo.pageRank over BUILDS_ON, mastered-set frontier computation, dated MASTERED edges and Goal/Objective persistence.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Epistemic outcome taxonomy (answered_with_path / answered_from_memory / not_in_graph / unknown)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Every tool resolves each named entity against the graph first; unknown entities short-circuit with 'unknown' and nothing runs, and a missing edge returns 'not_in_graph' with an explicit statement that this is a gap in the maps, not a finding. Each result carries the hops walked and a per-call trace (args, time, rows).

implemented_capabilities.capability: Graph-grounded goal drafting with LLM-phrase verification
implemented_capabilities.notes: Goal structure (baseline, one-grade-up goal, objectives, aligned standard) is computed from graph paths. A model (Gemini, optional) may only reword a standard as a skill phrase; check_skill rejects phrases that name standards not on the path, add numbers, use pronouns or add capitalised words, falling back to the standard's own text. Checks are logged per phrase.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Per-tenant graph isolation and privacy allowlist audit
implemented_capabilities.notes: One FalkorDB graph per district (staircase:<tenant>, regex-validated). Student IDs must match an opaque-ID regex before any write; audit_graph checks every Student node and MASTERED edge property against an allowlist via ro_query.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Keyword-router / Gemini tool-calling agent and MCP server
symbols: mcp tools (list_subareas, baseline_options, staircase, frontier, group_students, foundations, path_between, recall, draft_goal)
implemented_capabilities.notes: The public demo runs with a regex/keyword router (no model). With GEMINI_API_KEY the model picks from a fixed tool catalogue and never sees Cypher; arguments are re-validated by the tools.

graph_models_and_cypher: FalkorDB graph per tenant 'staircase:<district>'. Labels: Standard{id,grade,gi,description,level,subject,strand}, SubArea{key,label,area,subject,minGrade,maxGrade}, Student{sid,grade}, Goal{gid,created,session,text}, Objective{n,text}. Edges: PROGRESSES_TO, BUILDS_ON, RELATED, PART_OF, IN_SUBAREA, MASTERED{at,session}, FOR, STARTS_FROM, TARGETS, ALIGNS_TO, OF, PRACTICES. Uses shortestPath(), variable-length paths, algo.pageRank('Standard','BUILDS_ON'), UNWIND/MERGE, FOREACH conditional create. No APOC/GDS. Values are bound params except one clamped-int depth interpolation.
algorithms: Variable-length predecessor walk (depth 1..3) and shortestPath climb to the student's grade with fallback to the furthest reachable grade (tools.py:staircase)
Mastered-prerequisite frontier and shared-next-step student grouping (tools.py:frontier, group_students)
Rule-based verification of model-generated phrases against the graph path (goal.py:check_skill)
backend_interfaces: MCP stdio server (python -m staircase.mcp_server), 9 typed tools
frontend_interfaces: Static page (static/index.html, app.js, style.css) showing goal cards, staircase paths and a per-call tool trace
agent_or_memory_mechanisms: Dated student memory in the graph: MASTERED edges (at, session) and saved Goal nodes linked STARTS_FROM/TARGETS/ALIGNS_TO standards, returned as answered_from_memory with dates. Goals are drafted read-only and persisted only by a separate save call (teacher acceptance). Graph is rebuilt on container start in the public demo, so memory is not durable there.
tests_present: tests/test_staircase.py with 14 tests against a live FalkorDB (README): seed counts vs source JSON, path hops verified against the source JSON rather than the graph, tenant isolation, privacy refusal of name-like IDs, phrase-check rejections.
security_findings: app.py:~25-36,43-150 - no authentication on any route; district names are regex-validated and can be restricted with the STAIRCASE_DISTRICTS allowlist (public deploy sets it to 'demo'), but if unset any caller can create/read any staircase:<district> graph and write students, mastery and goals (MAX_STUDENTS cap only)
staircase/tools.py:198 - f-string interpolates depth into the variable-length range after int() clamp to MAX_DEPTH (safe as written)
staircase/goal.py:~60-80 - sends standard text to Gemini when GEMINI_API_KEY is set (external network call); failures are swallowed and fall back silently
data/ela.json (~589 KB) and data/math.json (~408 KB) - third-party Common Core / Achieve the Core derived content; redistribution terms are not stated in the repo and need verification before reuse
No eval/exec/pickle/subprocess found in staircase/ or app.py; no hard-coded secrets (.env.example is empty-valued)
duplicates_or_overlaps: Domain is unique in this batch (special-education IEP goal planning). The prerequisite-path/frontier logic overlaps Mobility & Accessibility learning-path style repos and software-dependency 'what must exist first' traversals; the entity-resolve-then-query guard overlaps generic anti-hallucination tool wrappers.
evidence_drift_relevance: MEDIUM - explicit unknown vs not_in_graph vs answered_from_memory outcomes with hop-level provenance, dated memory edges, accept-then-save gating and deterministic checking of LLM output against graph facts are good patterns for an Evidence Drift engine, though there is no supersession or dependency invalidation.

strongest_reusable_unit.why: Small pure-Python patterns: resolve-before-query with a four-way epistemic outcome, per-call trace, rule-based verification of model text against graph-derived allowed identifiers, and a property-allowlist audit of stored data.
strongest_reusable_unit.external_runtime_needed: FalkorDB for the tools; Gemini key only for optional phrase rewriting

strategy_rationale: The IEP/Common Core domain and bundled third-party standards data do not belong in Kairos and there is no license file, but the outcome taxonomy, LLM-output grounding check and tenant-per-graph privacy audit are worth re-implementing as patterns.
